sections.html: The 2025 population estimate is 171,666, up 11.6% from 153,843 in 2020. Owners occupy 85.2% of the 90,919 housing units, and median home value is $245,500. Seniors make up 38.1% of residents, so many owners watch their bills closely and plenty of sellers hold capped assessments.

The property appraiser handles valuation and exemption rulings here, while the tax collector sends the bill, takes payment and sells certificates.

  • Property appraiser: homestead and other exemption applications, portability, agricultural classification and the August TRIM notice. The office phone is (352) 341-6600.
  • Tax collector: bills, discounts, installment applications and delinquent tax advertising.
  • Clerk: files the deed at closing and collects stamp tax.

March 1 is the yearly cutoff for portability, exemptions, classifications and assessment reductions, and April 1 for tangible personal property returns. Owners who buy a home after January 1 are encouraged to pre-file for the next year.

The 4% November discount is the best of the year. It falls by one point each month, and March carries the gross amount, due by March 31.

Citrus County real estate tax calendar
MonthWhat happens
NovemberCollection begins; best discount through November 30
December3% discount; third installment due December 31
January2% discount
February1% discount
MarchLast day to pay; final installment due
AprilDelinquent from April 1, with a penalty
MayDelinquent list printed in the local paper, cost added
JuneCertificate sale starts

Quarterly payments spread the bill over the year. The application must reach the collector by April 30, and eligibility turns on prior year taxes above $100.

June 30 is the first due date, at 6% off, and a payment taken between July 1 and July 30 gets no discount. September 30 brings the second at 4.5% off and December 31 the third at 3% off. The fourth, due March 31, has no discount. If the first payment is missed, the plan ends and the full tax is due by March 31.

Payments one and two follow last year's bill. Ownership, value or exemption changes show up in payments three and four. Enrollment renews itself each year. A buyer taking over an active plan should check with the office, and the contract should say who pays each remaining installment.

A bill turns delinquent on April 1, with a 3% penalty on the gross amount.

In May the collector prints the delinquent list in the local newspaper weekly for three weeks, and that cost lands on the bill. Sale of certificates begins by June 1. Unpaid tangible personal property carries a 1.5% penalty after April 1 and is advertised once.

A tax deed application becomes possible two years after the certificate's issue date. Redemption stays open until a deed issues, and the opening bid on a homestead parcel includes half the assessed value. Request a payoff before listing, and keep the written figure with your closing file.

Homestead exemption can reduce taxable value by up to $50,000 if the county appraiser has your application before the March 1 cutoff.

The first $25,000 reduces every tax, and a second $25,000 reduces only non-school taxes on assessed value over $50,000. The appraiser puts typical savings at roughly $500 a year. After the first year, the assessment can't rise by more than the lesser of CPI change or 3 percent. If you moved from one Florida homestead to another within three years, you may be able to take some of your Save Our Homes savings along.

Homestead ends if the owner rents the unit or stops living there permanently, and a sale resets value to just value the next January 1. Furniture and equipment used in a rental or business is taxed separately as tangible personal property.

sections.h2: Relief for older and veteran owners
sections.html:
With seniors more than a third of the population, relief programs matter here. An ordinance can add a senior exemption of as much as $50,000 for older owners under an income cap. Ask the appraiser's office whether one applies locally.

  • Deferral: send Form DR-570 to the collector by March 31. It postpones the part of the tax above 5 percent of household income, or above 3 percent for permanent residents 65 and older.
  • Disabled veterans: $5,000 off assessed value at a service-connected rating of 10 percent or higher.
  • Veterans past 65 with a permanent service-connected disability can receive a homestead discount matching their VA percentage.

A denied exemption can go to the value adjustment board, but the petition window is 30 days.

At the table, the title company apportions the year's tax and pays any back taxes from your proceeds.

The recorded deed carries Florida stamp tax, 70 cents per $100 of price, and both buyer and seller stay liable. The first bill a buyer receives often differs from your last. Before closing, ask for three things.

  • A written payoff covering the current year and any earlier balance.
  • Word on whether a certificate was sold against the parcel.
  • The standing of any installment plan, which renews each year.

sections.h2: Steps for a Citrus County seller
sections.html: Gather your latest bill, any installment notice and your homestead paperwork. Call the collector for the payoff, then give the figure to your title agent so it can be matched against the settlement statement. If taxes are behind, expect the payoff to include the penalty and advertising costs. A cash sale skips lender underwriting, which can shorten the timeline, but the tax lien still has to clear at closing.

faqs.q: What is the Citrus County early payment discount?
faqs.a: It starts at 4% for November and drops a point each month through February. Nothing comes off in March, and April 1 begins delinquency.

faqs.q: When is the installment application due in Citrus County?
faqs.a: Applications close April 30. The first payment is due June 30, and a payment in July earns no discount.

faqs.q: When does a Citrus County tax bill turn delinquent?
faqs.a: On April 1, with a 3% penalty on the gross amount. A certificate sale starts by June 1.

faqs.q: What is the homestead filing deadline in Citrus County?
faqs.a: Get the form to the appraiser by March 1. The appraiser, not the collector, rules on eligibility.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Citrus County house that has delinquent tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company deducts whatever is owed from your sale proceeds, so get a payoff early and find out if the county sold a certificate.
